latin_text: Οἷά τις πτηνὸς αἰθέριος ὁ Παῦλος διέθει, κύκλῳ διατρέχων τὴν οἰκουμένην. Nicephor. Callist. ecclesiast. histor. lib. 3. cap. 1. καθάπερ ὑποπτερός τις πᾶσαν διαδραμὼν τὴν οἰκουμένην ἐσαγήνευσε. Menæa Græc. Jun. 29.

translation_history.english: Like some winged creature of the air Paul sped along, coursing in a circle through the inhabited world. Nicephorus Callistus, Ecclesiastical History, book 3, chapter 1. As if winged, having traversed the whole inhabited world, he caught it in his net. Greek Menaia, June 29.
translation_history.notes: Both Greek snippets stand alone without Latin paraphrase, so translated per Rule 1. ἐσαγήνευσε rendered as the Patristic image of catching souls as in a dragnet.

latin_text: Πᾶσαν σχεδὸν τὴν γῆν διελθὼν, καὶ ἐπὶ πέντε καὶ τριάκοντα ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ διαθλεύσας ἐνιαυτοῖς. Niceph. hist. eccles. lib. 12. cap. 34. Vix triginta annorum spatio et Romanos, et Persas, et Parthos, et Medos, et Indos, et Scythas, et Sauromatas, et Sarracenos, et omne prorsus humanum genus sub jugum mitteret veritatis, &c. Chrysost. homil. 4. de laudib. Pauli. Clemens in epistola ad Corinthios pag. 8. de eodem: Κῆρυξ γενόμενος ἐν τῇ ἀνατολῇ καὶ ἐν τῇ δύσει, τὸ γενναῖον τῆς πίστεως αὑτοῦ κλέος ἔλαβεν δικαιοσύνην διδάξαι ὅλον τὸν κόσμον, καὶ ἐπὶ τὸ τέρμα τῆς δύσεως ἐλθὼν, καὶ μαρτυρήσας ἐπὶ τῶν ἡγουμένων, οὕτως ἀπηλλάγη τοῦ κόσμου. In oriente ac occidente verbi præco factus, illustrem fidei suæ fainam sortitus est, in justitia mundum universum instruens, et ad occidentis terminos veniens, et sub imperatoribus martyrium subiens, sic e mundo migravit.

translation_history.english: Having traversed nearly the whole earth, and having contended for Christ through the gospel for five and thirty years. Nicephorus, Ecclesiastical History, book 12, chapter 34. Within scarcely thirty years' span he would bring under the yoke of truth the Romans, the Persians, the Parthians, the Medes, the Indians, the Scythians, the Sarmatians, the Saracens, and the entire human race outright, etc. Chrysostom, homily 4, "On the Praises of Paul." Clement, in the epistle to the Corinthians, page 8, on the same: Κῆρυξ γενόμενος ἐν τῇ ἀνατολῇ καὶ ἐν τῇ δύσει, τὸ γενναῖον τῆς πίστεως αὑτοῦ κλέος ἔλαβεν δικαιοσύνην διδάξαι ὅλον τὸν κόσμον, καὶ ἐπὶ τὸ τέρμα τῆς δύσεως ἐλθὼν, καὶ μαρτυρήσας ἐπὶ τῶν ἡγουμένων, οὕτως ἀπηλλάγη τοῦ κόσμου. Becoming the herald of the word in the East and in the West, he obtained illustrious fame for his faith, instructing the whole world in righteousness, and coming to the limits of the West, and undergoing martyrdom under the emperors, he thus departed from the world.
translation_history.notes: Third citation pairs Greek with a Latin paraphrase, so Greek is carried verbatim and only the Latin is rendered, per Rule 1. 'fainam' read as a printer's error for 'famam' (fame). 'Sauromatas' normalized to 'Sarmatians' per Rule 3.
